prompt: Create a precise sparse Chinese heritage INK LINE DRAWING of a representative surviving STONE DECK SEGMENT of Anping Bridge (安平桥 / 五里桥) in Quanzhou Fujian, seen at a low three-quarter perspective looking along the walkway. Image 1 and image 2 are real subject photos showing worn broad granite slab pavement, repeated low square stone railing posts with rectangular connecting rails, and a very long flat stone bridge receding into distance; image 3 only gives fine black-line illustration style. Preserve the characteristic FLAT stone beam bridge, no arches, and the rhythmic railing posts; show a few robust masonry piers and exposed long stone beams under the near side in a plausible simple side opening if visible. Depict a representative segment, not all 2.25 km or an invented exact pier count. Remove modern towers, river, signs, trees, sky, tourists and temples, isolating bridge masonry. Avoid textual markings. Fine charcoal contours and sparse slab joints, no filled black. Center in landscape 4:3 with generous margins. All canvas outside stone and true gaps must be flat opaque PURE WHITE #FFFFFF, no gray background, water, shadow, paper grain, gradient, glow, checkerboard or transparency.
